variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Assignment uses `:=`. The semicolon `;` or colon `:` ends statements, where `:` suppresses output.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Maple handles exact rational arithmetic and arbitrary precision floating point automatically.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: `mod` for modular arithmetic. `.` is used for matrix/non-commutative multiplication.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Standard if block ending with `end if;`.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Loops use `from ... to ... do ... end do;`.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: Standard while structure using `while ... do ... end do;`.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Procedures `proc` allow complex logic and type checking `::`. The arrow `->` creates simple mappings.

arrays.title: Arrays & Vectors
arrays.notes: Lists `[]` are immutable. `Vector` and `Matrix` from the LinearAlgebra package provide numerical arrays.

maps.title: Tables (Maps)
maps.notes: Tables provide associative array functionality in Maple.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Maple uses `try ... catch string_pattern: ... end try;` to handle exceptions selectively.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in Maple
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: Maple uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: Maple is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: Maple provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: Maple converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: Maple treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Maple formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: Maple executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: Maple indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: Maple emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in Maple
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: Maple uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: Maple stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: Maple uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: Maple provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: Maple loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
